# clavis lease setup

<p class="cli-lead">Set up a PostgreSQL, MySQL, or AWS STS credential source</p>

<div class="cli-usage">

```sh
clavis lease setup [flags]
```

</div>

Also available as `config-create`.

Set up a credential source: a Postgres or MySQL server and the grant to apply, or an AWS role to assume. Prints the config ID that `lease create` and `lease run` take. (Formerly `lease config-create`, which still works.)

## Examples

<p class="cli-example-title">Postgres</p>

```sh
clavis lease setup --host db.internal --database app \
  --username clavis_admin --password "$PGPASSWORD" \
  --grant-role app_readwrite --default-ttl 3600 --max-ttl 86400
```

<p class="cli-example-title">MySQL or MariaDB</p>

```sh
clavis lease setup --engine mysql --host db.internal --port 3306 \
  --database app --username clavis_admin --password "$MYSQL_PASSWORD" \
  --grant-privileges "SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE" --default-ttl 3600
```

<p class="cli-example-title">AWS STS</p>

```sh
clavis lease setup --engine aws --aws-region eu-central-1 \
  --aws-access-key "$AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID" --aws-secret-key "$AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY" \
  --aws-role-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/deploy
```

## Details

AWS leases return `access_key_id`, `secret_access_key`, `session_token`
and `expiration`; STS credentials can't be renewed, so create a new
lease. MySQL users have no database-side expiry: Clavis drops them when
the lease is revoked or when the expiry job runs.
